owner_creation.analysis: The literal private lbool owns the one-shot request to insert the next character literally; cmd_reset clears it and editor action 19 sets it.
owner_creation.invariant: Literal mode is one pending input interpretation decision.
limitations: literal owns a next-character interpretation flag.

aliases_escapes.analysis: literal retains no character pointer; cmd_char2 consumes completed bytes from the separate multibyte staging buffer before insertion.
aliases_escapes.invariant: Mode state does not own staged character bytes.
limitations: The flag must describe the same command sequence as cp and cmdbuf.

callback_targets.analysis: When true, cmd_char2 skips normal edit-command decoding and directly calls cmd_ichar; no function pointer is stored in the literal mode bit.
callback_targets.invariant: Literal interpretation selects data flow, not a callback.
limitations: Direct key processing stores no callback target in literal.

invalidation.analysis: Reset or consumption clears it, but the literal bit has no generation tying it to a particular command or partially assembled UTF character.
invalidation.invariant: Mode validity depends on the active editing operation.

mutation_commit.analysis: cmd_char2 clears the flag before cmd_ichar may reject a full buffer, so literal intent can be consumed without a committed text insertion.
mutation_commit.invariant: Consuming a mode is distinct from committing command bytes.

release_pair.analysis: The literal Boolean owns no heap or FD; clearing it must not release the multibyte array or command buffer used by the next stage.
release_pair.invariant: Literal-mode retirement releases no byte storage.
limitations: Consuming literal mode retires no heap object.

error_cleanup.analysis: literal is cleared before cmd_ichar may reject capacity, so a failed byte insertion does not automatically restore the consumed interpretation mode.
error_cleanup.invariant: A failed insertion does not restore literal intent automatically.

signals_handoff.analysis: As raw shared editor state, the literal bit relies on ordinary command sequencing and does not authorize nested handler-time command editing.
limitations: Source-specific review of coupled legacy editor state; M0-MEM-001 remains open and no new runtime defect is asserted from raw-pointer structure alone.

src/signal.rs.relationship: The terminate handler at src/signal.rs:83-85 has no literal-mode access. It marks the asynchronous termination boundary; a reentrant change to the next-character flag remains untraced.
